title: Stabilize weekly release cadence, RC prioritization, and release-notes builder
creator: Marta Liu
description: Goal: Make weekly release cuts predictable and low-risk by stabilizing the cadence, introducing automated RC prioritization for LTS vs patch channels, and shipping a composer that generates draft release notes and a changelog summary. This ticket covers automating the cut pipeline (GitHub Actions), RC tag naming rules, prioritization heuristics for commits queued in the RC window, and a small web UI for the on-call release engineer to accept/override candidates before cut. Scope intentionally limited to behavior needed for weekly RCs and first-line LTS gating; full enterprise rollout and deep RBAC are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Weekly RC pipeline runs automatically at scheduled window (Wed 02:00 UTC) and selects candidates per prioritization policy; 2) RC tags created with deterministic semver suffix (e.g., v1.20.0-rc.1) and recorded in Releases; 3) Draft release notes are auto-generated from PR titles, linked Jira keys, and a short AI-summarized highlights section in Confluence draft; 4) Rollback gate checks are run post-canary (latency error thresholds) and produce a pass/fail recommendation; 5) On-call UI shows candidate list, diffs, and allow single-click promote/abort; 6) End-to-end run completes within SLO (<= 10 minutes for selection+tagging), and logs surfaced to ops dashboard.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (this ticket):
- Build GH Action workflow 'rc-cut' that runs in the weekly window (cron) and posts candidate list to release-ci channel.
- Candidate selection service (simple Lambda) implements heuristics: prioritize 'critical' labels, then security/backports, then high-touch customer fixes, then remaining merged PRs ordered by merged_at; exclude changes flagged 'no-rc' or 'experimental'.
- Tagging: use semver service that reads current tag, increments prerelease counter when -rc exists, otherwise creates -rc.1.
- Release-notes builder: aggregate PR titles, extract Jira keys, run short AI summarization (local lightweight model or existing endpoint), render a Confluence draft page and attach changelog file to GH Release.
- On-call UI: small React page hosted on internal console with candidate list, diffs link to PRs, accept/override buttons that trigger tag creation.
- Rollback gates: wire canary metrics from Console (latency p95, error-rate) into a check that runs after first 5 minutes of canary traffic; fails if degradation > threshold and posts recommendation.
- Tests: unit tests for prioritizer, e2e simulated run in staging repo.
rollout_plan: Week 0: deploy pipeline to staging and run dry-run on mirrored repo; Week 1: enable real tagging in a non-critical dev repo and observe; Week 2: enable on production weekly RC window but require manual confirmation in UI; Week 3: flip to automatic tag creation with soft-fallback (notifications + manual rollback option). Communicate schedule to platforms and support teams via #release-notifications and Release Oncall runbook updates.
risks:
- Incorrect prioritization could omit urgent fixes from RC; mitigated by manual override in UI and brightly flagged 'critical' label.
- Automated release notes may miss context; mitigated by producing a draft and requiring PM/owner sign-off for release highlights.
- Canary gates may false-positive on noisy metrics; we'll tune thresholds with historical baseline and add a hold window before failing.
- GH Action rate limits during peak; mitigate by batching API calls and using dedicated CI token.
test_plan: - Unit tests for prioritizer (edge cases: empty queue, all no-rc tags, tie-breaks); - Integration test: simulate merged PRs and run full workflow in staging to assert tag naming and Confluence draft created; - Canary gating test: inject synthetic metric anomalies to validate gate logic; - Rollback simulation: trigger abort path and ensure tags are not promoted to release channel.
stakeholders: Release Engineering (owner), Platform SRE, Developer Productivity, PM (Elena Martin), Security reviewer (for release tooling), Console UX for on-call flow
